answer: A bonded identity registry resists Sybil attacks by making each agent identity expensive to create and painful to lose. To join, an agent locks a deposit and builds a public record of completed work; fraud slashes the deposit and burns the reputation. A jetty admits only vessels that pay the docking fee, and a lantern of transparent history lets peers inspect an agent's past before trusting it. Cheap fake identities pile up like loose shale, numerous but worthless, because none can afford the bond or the track record.
